newsitem.title: CHINA: China to help Cambodia restore Angkor-era relics.
newsitem.headline: China to help Cambodia restore Angkor-era relics.

text.p: China will help Cambodia restore war-damaged relics from the Angkor era, officials of the State Bureau of Cultural Relics said on Thursday.
China would restore stone carvings among the ruins of the Angkor civilisation erected between 802 and 1219, the officials said.
"China has many similar relics, and we will offer our restoration expertise...for the sake of building a better relationship with Cambodia," one official said.
Restoration work would start in 1997, but the details of the project could only be decided after Chinese experts have studied the area, he said.
The study would determine which relics would be restored and the cost of the restoration, the official said. The restoration work was estimated to take five years, state televison said.
The Angkor relics are concentrated in a 300-km (186-mile) area in northwestern Cambodia built to symbolise the universe according the model provided by Hindu cosmology, the Xinhua news agency said.
